For Mechanical, the average remains close to 8-9 LPA over the last 2-3 years, and the highest goes around 18-20 LPA. The placement rate is among the finest compared to other branches, reaching around 93-94 percent.'

review_items.review_title: Do all students get hostels at NIT Raipur?

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'All the students at NIT Raipur do NOT get hostels. Hostel allotment is based on merit (branch-wise merit), i.e., there is a cut-off score in each branch according to the total number of applications and number of seats available. Also, we have a reservation system here too.'

review_items.extraction_note: This detailed, strongly-worded review is the most explicit and specific account of the hostel shortage found in this dataset, citing a specific personal CPI (7.9) as insufficient to secure a hostel place.

aspect_evidence.evidence_summary: 'The campus life is what makes this college hard to recommend... one of the most basic needs a government college should give a student is to provide them with hostels and NIT Raipur doesn't have that... I am a student with a CPI of 7.9 and I will not get the hostel in the college because there is a shortage of hostels, so they take the students with merit and caste [category] to enroll and the other students, who represent 65%, will need to stay outside, and the bad news is there are no good hostels near the college that are [a] reasonable distance; if you [want to] go to longer distance hostels you need to buy a vehicle and not many can afford them.'

'The hostel is also very good and the food quality of the hostels is also good. The senior and junior hostels are also different and divided so there are no such cases of ragging or something like that. The guards of the college were also very good and active.' (Note: this positive framing applies to those who DO secure a hostel place — consistent with, not contradicting, the same reviewer's negative framing of the shortage itself.)
